newsitem.title: INDIA: Banks seen cutting prime rates by 1 pct point - RBI.
newsitem.headline: Banks seen cutting prime rates by 1 pct point - RBI.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor said on Saturday he expected banks to reduce their prime lending rates by at least one percentage point.
Chakravarty Rangarajan was replying to questions at a press conference where he outlined the RBI's monetary policy for the second half of 1996/97 (April-March)
"At least by one percent (-age point) immediately," Rangarajan told a questioner at a news conference after the policy announcement.
He said every reduction in cash reserve ratio (CRR) increased banks' lendable resources.
"It also increases their profits. All I am saying is pass on part of it," he said. The prime lending rate of banks in India range between 15.5 percent to 19 percent.
